justification: Fixes a cross-property mix-up in the conveyancing report: run_conveyancing trusted a caller-supplied (prop_id, lat, lng) triple without binding the parts, so prop_id-keyed data (LEP controls, valuation) and coordinate-keyed data (overlays, strata, nearby DAs) could describe two different properties under one address label. The trusted fast path is removed; _resolve_property derives prop_id, coordinates AND lot_wkt from the single resolve_address(req.address) call (which also enforces GATE-0 parcel identity). This also fixes the fast path leaving lot_wkt None (adversarial finding #3: overlay point-queries missed edge-only layers). Operational resolver failures now return 503 (retryable) rather than a 422 that blames a valid address.

pre_impl.existing_data: Reuses the existing resolve_address (scripts/generate_conveyancing_report.py), which already returns prop_id, lat, lng and lot_wkt bound to one address and enforces GATE-0 parcel identity fail-closed. No new data source, query, or fetcher is introduced; the change only stops bypassing that resolver.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Checked the frontend: ConveyancingTool posts only {address} to /conveyancing, so the removed caller-triple fast path was never exercised by the product — only reachable by direct API callers. The triple the frontend later sends to the PDF endpoint comes from this call's authoritative result, so it stays consistent.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New: the _resolve_property helper and the 503-vs-422 failure split. Deliberately unchanged: resolve_address itself, the parallel controls/overlays fetch, and the downstream response shape. The /conveyancing/pdf endpoint has the same caller-triple pattern but is mitigated by the report_id cache (authoritative first-call values) and the frontend flow; flagged for a follow-up, not changed here.

functions.name: _resolve_property
functions.input: the ConveyancingRequest — its address is authoritative; any caller-supplied prop_id, lat and lng are treated as advisory only and never used to fetch data
functions.output: a bound (prop_id:int, lat:float, lng:float, lot_wkt:Optional[str]) tuple all derived from resolve_address(req.address), so prop_id-keyed and coordinate-keyed data always describe the same property
functions.if_none: raises HTTPException 422 when resolve_address returns None (address not found or GATE-0 identity mismatch) and 503 when resolve_address raises (Portal outage); a caller prop_id disagreeing with the resolved one is logged and the resolved value wins

values: N/A - this diff reads no DB or API values directly; resolve_address (unchanged) performs the NSW Planning Portal /address and /lot calls.
queries: N/A - no SQL is written or changed in this diff.

break_it.scenario: A direct API caller posts an address for property B but a prop_id (and coordinates) belonging to property A.
break_it.what_happens: The old fast path trusted the triple, so LEP controls and valuation were fetched for A while overlays, strata and nearby DAs were fetched for B, and the whole mixture was labelled as B — a conveyancing report describing two different properties.
break_it.how: _resolve_property ignores the caller triple and derives prop_id and coordinates from resolve_address(req.address); the caller prop_id is only logged on disagreement. Everything is keyed to the one resolved property.

break_it.scenario: A caller supplies a prop_id and coordinates so the report is generated for a large battleaxe or irregular parcel.
break_it.what_happens: The old fast path left lot_wkt None, so get_unique_overlays / fetch_heritage_postgis ran a point query at the centroid and could miss a flood or heritage overlay intersecting only an edge of the parcel, yielding a plausible false clear.
break_it.how: resolve_address returns the parcel polygon WKT, which _resolve_property always passes through, so overlay queries test the whole lot geometry rather than a single point.

break_it.scenario: The address cannot be resolved to a parcel (not in the Portal index or a GATE-0 street-identity mismatch) while the caller still supplied a plausible-looking triple.
break_it.what_happens: Trusting the triple would emit an authoritative report for an unverified parcel that may not match the requested street address at all.
break_it.how: resolve_address returns None in this case and _resolve_property raises HTTPException 422 (fail closed) instead of falling back to the caller triple.

break_it.scenario: The NSW Planning Portal is unreachable or returns a 5xx while resolving a perfectly valid address.
break_it.what_happens: The previous blanket except mapped the operational error to HTTP 422 'could not resolve address', telling the user their valid address is invalid and giving no signal to retry.
break_it.how: resolve_address raising is caught and re-raised as HTTPException 503 with a retry message and logger.exception, distinct from the 422 not-found path.
